analysis.title: CoreWeave (CRWV): Core-We've got bills to pay... lowering our PT
key_insights: Bernstein stays Underperform on CRWV and cuts its price target to $51 from $74. The 21 Oct close was $61.82, implying 18% downside.
Bernstein estimates CRWV needs about $85B to deliver its existing committed backlog. $9B of that is covered by undrawn DDTL capacity, leaving roughly $76B of incremental financing to raise.

Unsecured bonds yield about 15%, which Bernstein reads as the market's required return for CRWV risk. It would not apply that yield mechanically to secured project-level facilities, but it raises the return hurdle for incremental investment.

Shifting to shorter-dated contracts and enterprise customers lets CRWV capture higher $/MW. Those contracts are riskier to creditors and do not lower its cost of capital. DDTL 5.5 priced at SOFR+5.5%, the best proxy, and later deals could price higher.

Secured debt remains the most viable funding source but depends on signing new contracts. Bernstein sees equity as a complementary and viable next step because secured debt alone cannot fund the backlog and growth plan.

Debt outstanding is $42.1B against $57.2B of total capacity, at a 7.8% effective rate and about $3.29B of annual interest expense. Most DDTL maturities fall in 2030-31, so Bernstein does not expect distress soon, but principal repayments and covenant tests start well before final maturity.

Bernstein's model has about $46B of growth capex next year to deliver the existing backlog, plus about $6B of maintenance capex. Stopping new contract wins would not quickly improve profitability because existing contracts still require funding.

Bernstein estimates a best-case unlevered IRR of 9-12% on the Meta contract, including the $21B expansion. Management says contracts signed from 2Q onward have materially better economics, but Bernstein thinks they are too small to change blended returns.
Bernstein assigns a low, nonzero probability to CRWV building a sufficiently differentiated enterprise business.

Bernstein does not think CRWV goes to zero because of its large backlog, line of sight to powered shell delivery, and contracts that are not underwater. It thinks NVDA would intervene in a true downside, which raises the floor without necessarily re-energizing the stock.

Bernstein views the risk as semi-contained. If CRWV ceased to exist, colo contracts would be absorbed and the rest of the market would carry on. Other neoclouds may be better placed on owned real estate, balance sheets, uncommitted 2027 capacity and non-US offerings, though Bernstein does not cover them.
The target multiple falls to 23.5x EV/EBIT from 25.5x, mainly on cost-of-capital concerns as contracts shorten. The PT rests on 23.5x NTM+1 adjusted operating income of $5.2B.
Bernstein cut its FY26E adjusted EPS to -$5.14 from -$4.56 and FY27E to -$6.81 from -$4.77. It forecasts FY26 revenue of $12.6B and FY27 revenue of $23.6B.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut from $74 as the multiple falls to 23.5x EV/EBIT on cost-of-capital concerns. About $76B of incremental financing is still needed to deliver the backlog.

sector_views.rationale: CRWV benefits from supply constraints, but Bernstein expects it to be among the first and hardest hit as capacity expands. It sees capital intensity, financing dependence and GPU residual value as sector-wide risks.

earnings_insights: Bernstein FY26E adjusted EPS is -$5.14, cut from -$4.56 (Bernstein estimate, not consensus). FY27E is -$6.81, cut from -$4.77. FY25A adjusted EPS was -$1.20 (reported).
Bernstein FY26E revenue is $12,622M and FY27E is $23,552M. FY26E EBITDA is $6,826M and FY27E is $14,974M (Bernstein estimates).

Bernstein FY26E operating income is $165M and FY27E is $2,478M. 3Q26E operating income is $77M, on revenue of $3,450M (Bernstein estimates). 2Q26 reported revenue was $2,575M and operating income was -$49M.
Bernstein's FY26E adjusted operating margin is 8.2% against consensus of 7.0%. For FY27E it is 15.6% against 15.5%.
Bernstein's 2026E capex is $35.7B and its 2027E capex is $48.5B, against consensus of $37.7B and $52.5B. Its no-future-backlog case is $37.7B in 2026E and $43.5B in 2027E.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Underperform call: delays in hyperscaler-built capacity keep CRWV's value proposition intact, CRWV's specialized software platform sustains demand, and a continued power shortage sustains its pricing power.
Cost of capital rises as CRWV moves to non-investment-grade enterprise customers and shorter contracts. DDTL spreads have widened to SOFR+5.5% on DDTL 5.5 from SOFR+2.25% on DDTL 4.0.
DDTL covenant tests start between Nov 2026 and Aug 2027, with DSCR thresholds of 1.15x to 1.35x on the active facilities.

Residual asset value is not reliable protection for equity holders. Recoveries depend on asset control, financing restrictions, pricing and capital structure priority. Training-optimized capacity may not suit Meta or OpenAI inference needs.
Competition from SPCX, hyperscalers and other neoclouds could pressure returns. CRWV has limited capacity to sell before 2028.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows CRWV gross debt to adjusted EBITDA on LTM and NTM bases, with values of 8.6x, 11.7x, 7.4x and 8.7x. The text does not label which value belongs to which basis.
Exhibit 6 shows DDTL spreads over SOFR: 4.25% on DDTL 2.0 and 2.1, 4.00% on 3.0, 2.25% on 4.0, 4.50% on 5.0 and 5.50% on 5.5.
Exhibit 7 shows capex estimates for 2026E to 2030E, with consensus at $35.7B, $48.5B, $50.8B, $55.2B and $62.9B.
Exhibit 5 shows the debt maturity schedule: $531M in 2026, $1,276M in 2027, $2,576M in 2028, $2,665M in 2029, $11,149M in 2030, $9,389M in 2031 and $10,334M in 2032.
vol_and_positioning: CRWV is down 27.6% over 1 month and 50.6% over 12 months. It trades near the low end of its 52-week range of $141.79 to $57.24, and at 65.7% relative underperformance against the SPX over 12 months.
Bernstein calls CRWV a wildly volatile, momentum-driven stock. Barring major moves, it sees the fundamentals as stuck.
cross_bank_references: Whether NVDA (covered by Rasgon) will step in is meatier; we think they would intervene in a true downside.

tension_points.bull_case: Shorter contracts and enterprise customers let CRWV capture higher $/MW, particularly if GPU spot pricing keeps rising. Newer contracts signed from 2Q are said to have materially better economics, and tight supply supports pricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Those contracts are riskier to creditors and do not lower the cost of capital. DDTL 5.5 priced at SOFR+5.5%, and the unsecured yield is about 15%. Newer contracts may be too small to change blended returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New contracts showing financing costs and capital requirements low enough to offset the pricing gains and lift overall returns, which Bernstein says it will watch for.

tension_points.bull_case: Large backlog, line of sight to powered shell delivery, and contracts that are not underwater. NVDA would likely intervene in a true downside, which raises the floor.
tension_points.bear_case: Residual asset value should not be relied on to protect equity holders. Recoveries depend on asset control, financing restrictions and capital structure priority.

theme_stances.key_argument: Funding the backlog is only part of the challenge, and the cost of that funding and the returns left for equity holders are the bigger questions.
theme_stances.evidence: funding the backlog is only part of the challenge

theme_stances.key_argument: Enterprise contracts improve pricing and diversification but bring weaker credit, shorter duration and higher financing costs.
theme_stances.evidence: Shorter contractual duration and weaker customer credit could make funding less attractive
